instruments.evidence: The capture uses the call's already-resumed context from openMicrophone, the one the Safari lesson in callRecorder requires.
CallMicrophone.context is set in the one place CallMicrophone is built, openMicrophone, and read only by the hook.
The modal tests drive the hook through the real modal and assert what reaches the socket, the player and the screen, not what the hook was called with.
The mocked socket and audio modules have the real modules' signatures, enforced by tsc on the test file.
A normal voice call connects with nothing pressed, streams out and plays back.
A server-ended socket shows an error rather than a frozen screen; a failure to connect or to start the capture does the same.
Mute while she is speaking stops what goes out and unmuting resumes it; the button is no longer disabled in that state.

The sibling start-call effect needed a StrictMode guard, because a double-invoked start made two calls. Asked the same of the live-connection effect: a close in its cleanup is a hang-up the server ends the call on. Added a StrictMode test and ran it against the unfixed code: one connection, never closed while mounted, because React double-invokes only on mount and the call id is still null then. Not a finding; the test stays as the guard.
The auto-listen loop, the recorder and the typing box are now reached only in video mode; the sentence-speech branch was reachable only in voice mode and is removed, not left dead.
Every failure path in the hook ends in onFailed, which the modal shows unless the user has already ended the call.
The live connection is gated on mode === 'voice' in the hook's arguments and the old loop on mode !== 'voice'; each test mode reaches only its own path.

The old voice path recorded call turns with recordCallTurn; that is now reached only from video. The Live path does not increment turn_count either, and nothing reads turn_count but the repository itself.
Unmounting closes the socket, stops the capture and clears the player, asserted in the first voice test; the microphone is released by the modal's own effect as before.

instruments.why: No finding, so nothing to control.
